Label.Tooltip: Glitchless: the seed can always be beaten without glitches. The logic is cautious, so it may expect an item a little earlier than you strictly need it. No Logic: items are placed completely at random; the seed may be unbeatable.

Label.Tooltip: Closed: as in the original. Mido blocks the Deku Tree until you have a sword and shield, and the Kokiri boy blocks the forest exit until the Deku Tree is beaten. Closed Deku: the forest exit is open from the start; Mido still wants a sword and shield. Open: both are out of the way; you can go to the Deku Tree or leave the forest right away.

ComboBox.Name: set_open_forest

Label.Tooltip: Open: the Door of Time in the Temple of Time is already open, so you can walk in and pull the Master Sword without the three Spiritual Stones, an ocarina or the Song of Time.

Label.Tooltip: Open: King Zora has already moved aside and stays aside, so Zora's Fountain and Jabu-Jabu can be reached without Ruto's Letter. Ruto still gives her reward in Jabu-Jabu. The quest log's Zora entry stays empty. Ruto's Letter would be useless, so it is replaced by an empty Bottle (wherever it lands, or at Lake Hylia if freestanding items aren't shuffled).

Checkbox.Name: set_open_dmt
Checkbox.Tooltip: The gate from Kakariko to Death Mountain is open for child Link from the start, so you don't need to show Zelda's Letter to the soldier. The Happy Mask Shop opens too, and the soldier's mask trade is ready. Zelda's Letter has no use then, so it isn't in the seed: a Red Rupee takes its place in the item pool, and Zelda gives a random item, also when quest rewards aren't shuffled.

Label.Tooltip: Child: a new game starts as child Link outside the Kokiri Shop, as always. Adult: a new game starts as adult Link on the pedestal platform in the Temple of Time, with the Master Sword, as if he had just pulled it. Rauru's check (the Light Medallion spot) is given at once, the Door of Time is open, and the Kokiri boy at the forest exit is gone, so child Link can get back into the forest. Put the Master Sword back to become a child. Random: child or adult, chosen by the seed (the spoiler log says which).

Label.Tooltip: What makes the rainbow bridge to Ganon's Castle appear when you walk up to the castle as adult. Every option also needs the Bow and the Light Arrows, since Ganon can't be beaten without them. Vanilla: as in the original. Beat the Shadow and Spirit Temples, get the Light Arrows from Zelda in the Temple of Time, then the sages build the bridge. Medallions: own the number of medallions set in Medallions Needed (any of the six), plus the Bow and the Light Arrows. Zelda's scene isn't needed. Spiritual Stones: own all three Spiritual Stones (Kokiri Emerald, Goron Ruby, Zora Sapphire), plus the Bow and the Light Arrows. Zelda's scene isn't needed. Gold Skulltula Tokens: own the number of tokens set in Gold Skulltula Tokens Needed, plus the Bow and the Light Arrows. Zelda's scene isn't needed. Once the bridge has appeared it stays. The altar in the Temple of Time tells the requirement and what you have of it (e.g. Medallions: 2/4).

Checkbox.Name: set_skip_child_zelda
Checkbox.Tooltip: A new save starts as if you had already been through Hyrule Castle as a child. You already own the items from Zelda (HC Zeldas Letter), Malon (HC Malon Egg) and Impa (Song from Impa), Malon and Talon are at Lon Lon Ranch, and Hyrule Field has day and night from the start. Those three checks can hold any item. Most come with the new save; bags, ammo, rupees, hearts, medallions and the like are handed over, with their item window, the moment a new game starts.

Checkbox.Name: set_skip_epona_race
Checkbox.Tooltip: Epona comes to you with just Epona's Song: play it as adult anywhere you can ride (Hyrule Field, Lon Lon Ranch, Gerudo Valley...). You don't need to race Ingo, or to have Malon's check at the ranch as a child first. Lon Lon Ranch and its race are left as they are. Needs a new save.
